_notice: ILLUSTRATIVE SEED CONTENT. Intervention descriptions reflect commonly used special-education practices but are NOT a curated clinical source. Effect sizes are assumed priors for simulation only. A domain expert must review, replace and cite real guidelines/literature before any real-world use.

interventions.name: Visual schedule
interventions.text: Provide a visual daily schedule with pictures or icons and preview changes in advance to support predictability and transitions.
interventions.parent_text: A picture schedule so your child knows what comes next and feels calmer.

interventions.name: Structured social skills instruction
interventions.text: Small-group, explicitly taught social skills sessions with modeling, role play and practice in natural settings.
interventions.parent_text: Small-group lessons that teach and practice friendship and conversation skills.

interventions.name: Low-stimulation workspace and sensory breaks
interventions.text: Offer a quiet, low-distraction workspace, noise-reducing options and scheduled sensory breaks.
interventions.parent_text: A calm spot and planned breaks so noise and lights are less overwhelming.

interventions.name: Proactive calming and de-escalation plan
interventions.text: Teach and rehearse a calming routine, identify early warning signs, and agree a consistent staff response to escalation.
interventions.parent_text: A shared plan for helping your child calm down early, before things escalate.

interventions.name: Scheduled movement breaks
interventions.text: Build short, scheduled movement breaks and active learning tasks into lessons.
interventions.parent_text: Short planned movement breaks so your child can release energy and refocus.

interventions.name: Chunked tasks with immediate feedback
interventions.text: Break assignments into short timed chunks with a checklist and immediate feedback or reinforcement after each chunk.
interventions.parent_text: Work is split into small steps with quick encouragement after each one.

interventions.name: Preferential seating and reduced distractions
interventions.text: Seat near the teacher and away from high-traffic or noisy areas; keep workspace uncluttered.
interventions.parent_text: A seat that helps your child stay focused.

interventions.name: Organisation and executive-function coaching
interventions.text: Teach planner use, checklists and routines for materials and homework, with regular check-ins.
interventions.parent_text: Help with planners and checklists so homework and materials stay organised.

interventions.name: Structured literacy (multisensory phonics)
interventions.text: Explicit, systematic, multisensory phonics instruction with phonological awareness practice delivered several times per week.
interventions.parent_text: Step-by-step reading lessons using sight, sound and touch to build decoding skills.

interventions.name: Extended time on reading-heavy tasks
interventions.text: Provide extended time and reduced reading load on assessments and in-class tasks.
interventions.parent_text: Extra time on reading and tests so your child can show what they know.

interventions.name: Text-to-speech and audiobooks
interventions.text: Provide text-to-speech software and audio versions of texts to access grade-level content.
interventions.parent_text: Audio versions of reading so your child can learn grade-level content.

interventions.name: Timed oral reading fluency drills
interventions.text: Repeated timed oral reading drills to build fluency.
interventions.parent_text: Timed reading practice to build speed.

interventions.name: Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
interventions.text: Introduce an AAC system (picture exchange, symbol board or speech-generating device) with communication-partner training.
interventions.parent_text: A tool such as picture cards or a talking device to help your child communicate.

interventions.name: Speech-language therapy integration
interventions.text: Coordinate regular speech-language therapy and embed targets into classroom routines.
interventions.parent_text: Speech therapy with practice built into the school day.

interventions.name: Visual supports for language comprehension
interventions.text: Pair spoken instructions with visuals, gestures and simplified language; check comprehension.
interventions.parent_text: Pictures and simple words alongside instructions to help understanding.

interventions.name: Larger, well-spaced text and reading guides
interventions.text: Use larger font, increased line spacing, uncluttered pages and a reading ruler or window to reduce visual crowding.
interventions.parent_text: Easier-to-read page layouts to help your child follow lines of text.

interventions.name: Functional vision / optometry referral
interventions.text: Refer for a functional vision or developmental optometry assessment if tracking or eye-strain difficulties persist.
interventions.parent_text: An eye check focused on how your child's eyes work together for reading.

interventions.name: Concrete-representational-abstract math instruction
interventions.text: Teach math using concrete objects, then drawings, then symbols, with explicit modeling and frequent review.
interventions.parent_text: Math lessons that start with hands-on objects before moving to numbers.

interventions.name: Calculator and math reference aids
interventions.text: Allow calculators, multiplication charts and worked-example references on appropriate tasks.
interventions.parent_text: Math tools like charts and calculators to reduce frustration.

interventions.name: Keyboarding and speech-to-text for writing
interventions.text: Teach keyboarding and provide speech-to-text so ideas are not limited by handwriting demands.
interventions.parent_text: Typing and voice tools so writing difficulty doesn't hide your child's ideas.

interventions.name: Occupational therapy for fine-motor and handwriting
interventions.text: Occupational therapy support for fine-motor control, grip and handwriting fluency.
interventions.parent_text: Occupational therapy to strengthen hand control for writing.

interventions.name: Clinician coordination on medication effects
interventions.text: Coordinate with the prescribing clinician; log classroom attention and side effects at agreed intervals and share them with the clinical team. School staff do not adjust medication.
interventions.parent_text: We will share classroom observations with your child's doctor; medication decisions stay with the doctor and you.

rules.why: Timed oral reading may heighten anxiety in a dyslexic student with anxiety; prefer untimed supports.
Transition difficulty in ASD is commonly addressed with visual schedules.
Minimal spoken language indicates AAC should be considered.
Clinician coordination is standard when medication is part of care.

synthesis.text: Provide a fixed, predictable home seat in a low-distraction area, plus scheduled and pre-announced movement breaks (e.g. errands, standing station) at set times.
Break tasks into short chunks with checklist and immediate feedback, but do not enforce time limits on reading-heavy chunks; allow extended time to finish each chunk.

policy_corpus.text: IEP goals must be measurable, with baseline, target, timeframe and measurement method.
policy_corpus.source: Seed policy rule (verify against applicable law, e.g. IDEA in the US or local equivalent)

policy_corpus.text: The plan must state present levels of academic achievement and functional performance.
Parents/guardians must be involved in developing the plan and informed in accessible language.
The plan must address education in the least restrictive environment appropriate to the child.
Plans are decision support only; a qualified human team must review and approve before implementation.
